# GridEditor

> **File:** `services/ui/GridEditor.qml` · **Docs:** see [docs/dev](../../README.md)

Editing of one grid of modules (each with a `place` { x, y, w, h } in quarter cards), shared by the layouts editor's overlay pages and edge menus. Not a singleton: OverlayManager and EdgeMenuManager each own one, point `modulesOf` at the live modules array in their draft and run their draft's changed() on `edited`. Also holds the selection, since the editor page is unloaded whenever the overlay closes. Every edit keeps the selection on its module and shifts the grid so its top left module sits at 0, 0: a place left of or above the grid (negative x or y) makes room there. A grid with an `area` (the lock screen's) is bounded instead: places are absolute, inside it. Required module types (`x-required`) are never removed or duplicated. Drops, moves and resizes are worked out first as a plan (planAdd, planMove, planResize), which the canvas shows while dragging and applyPlan() makes: a module put onto others pushes them along `pushDir`. Every edit can be undone (undo/redo; the owner calls clearHistory() when it reloads the modules).

### Properties

- `modulesOf` (var): Returns the modules array being edited (mutated in place), or null
- `host` (string): Where the modules are shown: "overlay", "edgeMenu" or "lockscreen" (x-hosts)
- `area` (var): A bounded grid ({ cols, rows }): modules stay inside it where they are put, and the grid never shifts. null: it grows and shifts back to 0, 0 after every edit
- `screenBox` (var): An edge menu's screen around its grid (GridPlacement.screenBox) and its edge: the screen along the edge is what its modules are centred on (guideFrame). null for a page or a submenu
- `edge` (string)
- `sizeScale` (int): How many of this grid's units make one of a card's quarters (2 on a doubled lock screen grid): new modules' default sizes scale by it
- `hold` (var): Axes ({ x, y }, each optional) on which a gap before the modules stays rather than being shifted away after an edit (a whole-edge menu's, along its edge: the gap is part of where it sits)
- `pushDir` (var): Which way modules a drop lands on are pushed ({ x, y }, one of them 1 or -1): down on a page, along an edge menu's edge
- `scopeKey` (string): What's being edited (a page, a menu): forms are rebuilt when it changes
- `shifted` (var): Called in every edit, as the grid shifts back to 0, 0: with the shift taken off ({ x, y } grid units, a place left of or above the grid being negative) and how far the modules reached before the edit…
- `selected` (readonly int): Index of the selected module, -1 for none (or for a group)
- `group` (readonly var): Indices of a group of modules selected together (two or more; a box dragged on the canvas, or Shift/Ctrl+click), else []: moved, nudged and removed together
- `canUndo` (readonly bool)
- `canRedo` (readonly bool)
- `snapshotExtra` (var): Owner state that edits change besides the modules (an edge menu's offset, which keeps it in place as its grid shifts): taken with every snapshot and put back with it
- `restoreExtra` (var)

### Signals

- `edited()`: After every edit: the owner marks its draft changed

### Functions

- `problemsFor(modules, name, area)`: Why these modules can't be saved as is, each prefixed with `name`, on a bounded grid of `area` ({ cols, rows }; this one's when left out)
- `defaultSize(type)`: A new `type` module's [w, h] on this grid
- `minSize(type)`: The least [w, h] a new `type` module dropped into a gap shrinks to
- `select(index)`
- `clearSelection()`
- `selectGroup(indices)`: Selects `indices` together: one is a plain selection
- `toggleSelected(index)`: Adds module `index` to the selection, or takes it out
- `isSelected(index)`
- `selection()`: The selection as indices: the group, the one selected, or []
- `module(index)`
- `selectedModule()`
- `canRemove(index)`: Whether module `index` may be removed or duplicated (not a required one)
- `planAdd(type, place)`: A new `type` module dropped at `place` (its default size, held by its middle unit, as GridPlacement.canvasDropPlace gives it): on a free cell, the most of its default size that fits there (down to it…
- `planMove(index, x, y)`: Module `index` moved with its top left to x, y: exactly onto a module of its size they swap, else it pushes what it lands on
- `planResize(index, place)`: Module `index` resized to `place` (GridPlacement.resizeFrom: any side may move), pushing what it grows onto
- `planMoveGroup(indices, dx, dy)`: The modules at `indices` moved together by `dx`, `dy` units (kept inside the `area`), pushing what they land on
- `guideFrame(places, exclude)`: What the modules at `exclude` are aligned and centred against, among `places` (GridPlacement.guideFrame): the `area`, else the other modules, an edge menu's screen along its edge
- `planCentre(axis)`: The selection centred across (`axis` "x") or down ("y") in its frame (guideFrame), as a plan (planMove / planMoveGroup; noop when it's centred already).
- `centreSelection(axis)`
- `canAdd(type, place)`: Whether a new module of `type` may be dropped at `place`
- `canMove(index, x, y)`: Whether module `index` may move with its top left to x, y
- `canResize(index, w, h)`: Whether module `index` may take the size w × h (top left kept)
- `undo()`
- `redo()`
- `clearHistory()`: When the edited modules are reloaded (the draft loaded or reset)
- `applyPlan(plan)`: Makes a plan (planAdd, planMove, planResize), if it's still valid for the modules as they are
- `addModule(type, place)`: A new module at its schema defaults: dropped at `place` when given (planAdd), else at its default size in the first free spot (refused when a bounded grid has none)
- `moveModule(index, x, y)`
- `resizeModule(index, place)`: To `place` ({ x, y, w, h }: a resize may move any side)
- `nudge(dx, dy)`: The selected module (or group) moved `dx`, `dy` units (the keyboard's arrows)
- `grow(dx, dy)`: The selected module's bottom right moved `dx`, `dy` units
- `duplicateModule(index)`: A copy at the same size in the first free spot
- `removeSelection()`: Every module selected (the group, or the one) but required ones
- `removeModule(index)`
- `recordField(field)`: Records an undo step before an edit to `field` (a module's property, or an owner's own setting kept in snapshotExtra); more edits to the same field (typing, a stepper) join it
- `updateModuleProperty(index, key, value)`
